title: HITL: Agent self-correction demo (capstone)
description:
## What to build

The capstone demonstration: an AI agent detects a cyclomatic complexity violation via the pre-tool-use hook and self-corrects without human intervention.

Sequence (spec Section 8, Step 3):
1. Task the agent with a feature in graft (Go, block mode) that will naturally cause a CC violation
2. Agent attempts to write the file → pre-tool-use hook fires → calm-bridge blocks with violation message
3. Agent reads the violation message, understands the constraint, and refactors
4. Agent re-attempts the write → hook passes → file written
5. Agent commits → pre-commit hook passes → commit succeeds

This proves the full loop: architectural governance enforced on AI agents at write-time, with the agent treating violations as actionable constraints rather than errors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Agent tasked with feature that naturally produces CC > threshold
- [ ] Pre-tool-use hook blocks the first write attempt
- [ ] Agent reads violation message from stderr
- [ ] Agent refactors to reduce CC below threshold without human guidance
- [ ] Second write attempt succeeds
- [ ] git commit succeeds (pre-commit hook passes)
- [ ] Entire sequence captured/recorded for demonstration
- [ ] Also demonstrated in C# (block mode, deferred pattern) and Python (advisory mode)

## Blocked by

- calm-poc-3n7 (HITL: Manual runbook validation)
- calm-poc-739 (Claude Code pre-tool-use hook)

title: AI Slop fitness functions (LDR + DDC)
description:
## What to build

Implement the two AI Slop detection fitness functions from spec Section 5.3:

**Logic Density Ratio (LDR)**: logic_lines / total_lines. Detects hollow, boilerplate-heavy AI-generated code. Logic lines = arithmetic, control flow, state mutation, function calls. Excluded: whitespace, comments, imports, type declarations, structural scaffolding.

**Dependency Discipline Check (DDC)**: used_imports / total_imports. Detects unused imports commonly left by AI agents.

Both are per-file metrics, deterministic, fast, and cross-language.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] LDR calculation implemented for all three languages
- [ ] Logic line classification correct per language (control flow, arithmetic, mutation, calls)
- [ ] DDC calculation implemented for all three languages
- [ ] Import usage detection: each import checked for at least one reference in file body

- [ ] Violation messages match spec Section 5.3 format (including unused import list for DDC)
- [ ] Unit tests: file with 90% boilerplate triggers LDR violation

title: Deep vs. Shallow fitness functions (interface width + implementation depth)

## What to build

Implement the two Deep vs. Shallow fitness functions from spec Section 5.2:

**Rule A — Interface Width Ceiling**: Maximum public methods per CALM node (module/package/namespace). A module with too many public methods imposes high cognitive cost.

**Rule B — Implementation Depth Floor**: Minimum average implementation LOC per public method. Modules with very little logic per public method are likely pass-through facades.

Both rules fire independently per module. Both use data already collected by the analyzers (public method count, LOC).

title: Enforcement mode routing + outstanding violation state
description:
## What to build

1. Read .calm/config.json from the target repository to determine enforcement-mode (block/advisory/off) and which fitness functions are enabled.
2. Route violations through the mode: block returns status=block with exit 1 intent, advisory returns status=advisory with exit 0 intent, off skips checks entirely.

- [ ] enforcement-mode=off: no analysis performed, returns status=pass
- [ ] Outstanding violations accumulate across calls and block until cleared
- [ ] Violations cleared when the offending file passes on re-check

title: Bridge /check endpoint: C# cyclomatic complexity with deferred first-call
description:
## What to build

Wire the full /check endpoint for C# files with the deferred first-call pattern from spec Section 2:

1. First call on a C# file when daemon is cold: return {"status":"pass","warming":true} immediately
2. Daemon warms Roslyn in background, analyzes the file just written
3. If violations found: store in state, keyed by file path
4. On next hook call in same repo: check state for outstanding violations and block

This pattern handles Roslyn's up-to-3s cold start without blocking the first write.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] POST /check with language=csharp on cold daemon returns pass+warming immediately
- [ ] Roslyn analyzer starts in background, analyzes the deferred file
- [ ] Violations stored in state map (repo → file → violations)
- [ ] Subsequent /check calls return block if outstanding violations exist
- [ ] After warm-up, subsequent C# checks are synchronous (no more warming:true)
- [ ] Integration test proving deferred-then-block pattern
- [ ] Integration test proving warm path is synchronous

title: Baseline: C# analyzer (Roslyn) against StackOverflow.Api.V3 and SlackStatus
description:
## What to build

Implement the C# language analyzer using a lightweight Roslyn CLI as a subprocess. The Roslyn CLI must be built as a separate .NET tool that emits JSON matching the AnalysisResult struct. Run it against both C# test repositories to produce baseline reports.

Note: Roslyn has a cold start of up to 3 seconds. This is acceptable for baseline runs but informs the deferred first-call pattern in the bridge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Roslyn analyzer CLI built as a .NET tool (separate project/subdir)
- [ ] Emits JSON matching AnalysisResult schema (CC per function, public methods, LOC, imports)
- [ ] C# analyzer wrapper implemented in internal/analyzer/csharp.go
- [ ] Invokes Roslyn CLI as subprocess, parses JSON output
- [ ] Returns normalized AnalysisResult struct
- [ ] Produces baseline-report-stackoverflow-api.json and baseline-report-slackstatus.json
- [ ] Unit tests with known-complexity C# fixture files
- [ ] Cold start time measured and documented

## Blocked by

- calm-poc-m5i (Scaffold Go module with CLI + daemon skeleton)
notes:
## Review Skills

When having the work reviewed as prompted, these are the skills to be used for the subagents:

**MUST:**
- test-driven-development
- dotnet-backend-patterns

**SHOULD:**
- dotnet-test-frameworks
- golang-error-handling
## Subagent review summary

Review cycle 1:
- /test-driven-development: Found that C# coverage used only a fake Roslyn executable and did not verify the real analyzer or C# baseline CLI path. Added real Roslyn integration tests, C# wrapper failure tests, and `calm-bridge baseline --language csharp --roslyn ...` coverage.
- /dotnet-backend-patterns: Found fresh C# baseline runs failed without manual `--roslyn`, and Roslyn only counted `MethodDeclarationSyntax`. Added repo-local auto-build for omitted `--roslyn`, .NET tool metadata, README guidance, and expanded Roslyn traversal to constructors, accessors, operators, local functions, and interface members.
- /dotnet-test-frameworks: Found missing real Roslyn integration coverage, missing CLI C# baseline coverage, missing tool packaging metadata, and missing cold-start documentation. Added all of these and measured Debug cold start at 0.12 seconds for a one-file fixture.
- /golang-error-handling: Initially could not be spawned because of thread limit; later spawned as required and found stdout/stderr mixing plus missing auto-build timeout semantics. Fixed with separated stdout/stderr capture, stderr context on parse failures, and `errors.Join` timeout preservation for auto-build failures.

Review cycle 2:
- /test-driven-development: Found tests did not uniquely prove interface member counting and did not force the auto-build branch. Fixed with a distinct interface-only member assertion, exact public method count, and a test that temporarily moves the built analyzer aside.
- /dotnet-backend-patterns: Found namespace `using` directives were reported unused when imported types were referenced, and local function branches were double-counted in containing methods. Fixed by using Roslyn semantic model namespace resolution and preventing nested function descendants from contributing to containing-function complexity.
- /dotnet-test-frameworks: No findings.
- /golang-error-handling: Found stdout/stderr mixing and auto-build timeout semantics. Fixed and verified with focused tests.

## Conflict resolution

Conflict: Require users to pass `--roslyn <path>` explicitly, or auto-build/use the repo-local analyzer for C# baselines.
Decision: Auto-build/use the repo-local analyzer when `--language csharp` and `--roslyn` is omitted, while preserving `--roslyn` for explicit tool paths.
Rationale: The acceptance criteria require a separate Roslyn CLI, and first-run baseline operability should work from the repo without relying on a preinstalled PATH command.

Conflict: Treat C# namespace imports as unused unless the namespace name itself appears, or use Roslyn semantic resolution to infer imported type usage.
Decision: Use Roslyn semantic model resolution for namespace imports and alias-name matching for aliases.
Rationale: Normal C# uses imported type names such as `StringBuilder`, not namespace segment names such as `Text`; semantic resolution avoids false unused-import baselines.

Conflict: Count nested local-function branches in both the containing method and the local function, or isolate complexity to each function node.
Decision: Isolate local-function complexity to the local function and exclude nested function descendants from containing-function complexity.
Rationale: Double-counting nested branches inflates baseline distributions and makes threshold calibration misleading.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/analyzer -run 'TestAnalyzeCSharpFile|TestWriteBaselineReport'`
- `go test ./cmd/calm-bridge -run 'TestRunBaseline'`
- `go test ./...`
- `go test -race ./...`
- `dotnet build tools/roslyn-analyzer/CalmRoslynAnalyzer.csproj --nologo`
- `dotnet pack tools/roslyn-analyzer/CalmRoslynAnalyzer.csproj --nologo`
- `./scripts/baseline.sh --repo /Users/poconnor/peter_code/SlackStatus --language csharp --output baseline-report-slackstatus.json --name SlackStatus`
- `./scripts/baseline.sh --repo /Users/poconnor/code/StackOverflow/StackOverflow.Api.V3 --language csharp --output baseline-report-stackoverflow-api.json --name StackOverflow.Api.V3`

## Next-task notes

`baseline-report-slackstatus.json` and `baseline-report-stackoverflow-api.json` now include explicit distributions and C# semantic import usage. Downstream governance work should calibrate thresholds from the regenerated reports.

## Subagent review summary

Review cycle 1:
- /test-driven-development: Found missing single-line parenthesized import coverage and missing explicit baseline distribution fields in `baseline-report-ringstation.json`. Fixed `pythonImportMetric`, added regression coverage, added `distributions` to baseline reports, and regenerated the reports.
- /python-testing-patterns: Found missing `radon raw` error payload coverage. Added `parseRadonRaw` and repository raw-error tests. Non-blocking observation: fake radon scripts are Bash even when named `.bat` on Windows.
- /golang-error-handling: Found missing cancellation semantics in `runTool` and missing malformed raw-output context in `parseRadonRaw`. Fixed by preserving `context.Canceled`/`context.DeadlineExceeded` through `errors.Join`, separating stdout/stderr, and adding trimmed malformed-output context.

Conflict: Keep Bash-only fake radon scripts for local tests, or add cross-platform Windows batch fixtures now.
Decision: Keep Bash-only fake radon scripts for this PoC and record Windows portability as non-blocking.
Rationale: The current project workflow and acceptance environment are local macOS/Bash, the production analyzer invokes configurable external tools, and the acceptance criteria do not require Windows test execution.

Conflict: Missing gocyclo/radon-derived data could be represented as zero metrics or omitted.
Decision: Omit unavailable/ignored function entries rather than synthesizing zero complexity.
Rationale: Zero complexity corrupts threshold distributions; omission preserves analyzer semantics for ignored or tool-skipped functions.

`baseline-report-ringstation.json` now includes explicit `distributions` arrays for threshold calibration. Downstream governance threshold work should use the summary percentiles and raw distributions, not scrape per-file `results`.

## What to build

Build the calm-bridge binary entry point with two modes from a single binary:

- **CLI mode**: `calm-bridge check [flags]` — auto-starts the daemon if not running, then delegates via HTTP POST to localhost:7890.
- **Daemon mode**: HTTP server on localhost:7890 with /health, /shutdown, /check (stub 200), /state (stub) endpoints.

The CLI should detect whether the daemon is already running (probe /health), start it in the background if not, and wait for readiness before forwarding the request.

title: Improve C# Dependency Discipline with project-aware import resolution
description:
## What to build

Upgrade the C# analyzer so Dependency Discipline can enforce meaningful thresholds instead of the current advisory/no-op `gte 0` baseline. The analyzer should load enough project compilation context for project-local namespaces and references, then recompute C# DDC baselines and propose a non-zero threshold.

## Context

During `calm-poc-d2g`, Peter explicitly approved the temporary Dependency Discipline threshold of `0` for the PoC only if project-aware C# import resolution is tracked as follow-up work. Current single-file Roslyn analysis resolves platform namespaces and aliases but cannot reliably resolve every project-local namespace import.

## Acceptance criteria

- C# analyzer accepts project or solution context when available
- Project-local namespace imports are resolved accurately enough for DDC calibration
- Unit/integration tests cover project-local namespace usage and unused imports
- SlackStatus and StackOverflow.Api.V3 baseline reports are regenerated
- `patterns/governance.json` is updated or a calibration recommendation is documented with a non-zero DDC threshold
- Review notes include findings from `/dotnet-backend-patterns`, `/golang-error-handling`, and `/test-driven-development`


## Required Skills
dotnet-backend-patterns,golang-error-handling,test-driven-development
